- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early forecast periods (first 10–15 days of 30d window).
- Forecasts tend to peak too early or too high after recent spikes, then sharply drop — suggesting overshoot and failure to capture mean reversion.
- Model underestimates prices in the final 5–10 days of the 30d window, particularly when true values show downward momentum.
- Forecast bias is stronger in low-price regimes (e.g., <70) — model tends to underestimate, while overestimating in high-price regimes (>75).
- Model exhibits lag in adjusting to recent price drops — often holds high forecasts even when true values are falling.
- Forecasts show poor sensitivity to recent volatility — fails to adjust to sharp reversals or sudden drops in price.
- Model tends to smooth out short-term volatility, leading to overly stable or “flat” forecasts that miss sudden price swings.
- In cases of prolonged price consolidation, model overestimates future price movement, assuming continuation of trend.
- Model underperforms when true price moves are driven by policy or regulatory changes — forecasts ignore external shocks.
- Forecasts are more accurate when price is trending upward — model struggles with downward trends or sideways movements.
